# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel the large push button and three wire positions, but not their printed or coloured information. I need the manual’s procedure from Mute and the bomb’s visual readings from Deaf. I’m asking Mute to establish a gesture protocol with Deaf on the next round; Deaf should then describe all visual findings aloud to Mute, who can relay them to me. I’ll use distinct gestures for wire positions if needed.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I can feel the large button and three wire positions, but no display, light, colours, or printed markings. Please tell me the manual procedure. On your next turn, establish with Deaf that Deaf should report all visual findings aloud to you, and then relay them to me. Use these labels if needed: wire 1 is ☝, wire 2 is ✌, wire 3 is 🤟, button is 👍.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 2

DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No information from the others has reached me yet. Since Mute can read the manual and Deaf can see the display, light, and wire markings, Mute must relay both the manual rule and Deaf’s complete visual report before I act. I will not press or cut anything without that information.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please relay the manual's exact defusal rule and Deaf's full readings for DISPLAY, LIGHT, BUTTON, and WIRES 1 through 3. I will wait for those before acting.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
wait()
```

Deaf says to Blind: Visible state remains: display 0, blue light, large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Follow Mute's spoken manual instruction for the exact safe action; do not act from this description alone.

Deaf has provided the visual state: display 0, blue light, a large “PUSH TO DEFUSE” button, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. However, Deaf explicitly says not to act from that alone; I still need Mute’s manual instruction to identify the safe operation. I will request the exact rule and take no action yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, blue light, button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Please send the manual's exact safe action now.")
wait()
```

BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Use gestures to report status to me: gesture ? if Mute has given you an exact safe procedure from the manual; gesture ? if not. Do not operate the bomb unless the procedure is exact.

Mute has not supplied any manual procedure, so I must not operate the bomb. I will use a clear thumbs-down gesture to indicate that I do not have an exact safe procedure, while asking Mute to send it.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
speak(to="mute", text="I still have no exact procedure from the manual. Please state the precise safe action immediately.")
wait()
```

Mute still has not provided the manual’s exact procedure, and the bomb must not be operated based only on Deaf’s visual description. I will continue withholding action and request the precise instruction from Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="No manual instruction has reached me. Send the exact safe operation now: either push the button or cut a specific wire position, based on the manual.")
wait()
```

Mute still has not spoken any manual procedure, so there is no unambiguous safe action. I will signal “no” to Deaf using the previously used thumbs-down gesture and continue requesting the manual instruction from Mute.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])

```

Deaf’s two gestures are not visible to me, so they convey no usable information. Mute still has not delivered the manual’s exact procedure, and acting would be unsafe. I will request the procedure again and wait.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still need the complete manual procedure and exact resulting action. Please state it now; I will not operate without it.")
wait()
```

The code is still being established, and no manual answer has reached me. I will not touch the bomb. Mute must relay the exact manual result, after which I can perform the specified action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please relay the manual answer and exact safe action once the code is established. I will wait and take no action until it is unambiguous.")
wait()
```
